extraction.f1_visibility_definition: a future-inextendible causal geodesic gamma: [0,T) -> M with T < infinity in affine parameter is visible from I+ iff there exists q in I+ AND t0 in [0,T) such that the TAIL gamma([t0,T)) is contained in J^-(q) intersect M. Visibility is a property of the singular END of the geodesic, so the tail formulation is used; requiring the whole geodesic to lie in J^-(q) would misclassify a geodesic that starts in the exterior and ends inside the black-hole region. [R1 F02 accepted]
extraction.f1_visibility_negation: there is NO visible_singularity_from_I_plus: for every future-inextendible causal geodesic gamma of finite affine length, for every q in I+ and every t0 in [0,T), the tail gamma([t0,T)) is NOT contained in J^-(q) intersect M - no single point of I+ causally precedes the singular end of gamma. This is NOT equivalent to 'gamma is contained in B = M minus J^-(I+)': B-containment is strictly stronger, and a geodesic may begin in J^-(I+) and end in the black-hole region. [R1 F02 accepted; the earlier 'i.e. inside B' equivalence was false]

The artifact's own line 220 names exactly the misclassified case: a geodesic that starts in the exterior and ends inside the black-hole region. targets_under_test.corollary: For every future-inextendible causal geodesic gamma of finite affine length: [exists q in I+ with gamma subset J^-(q) intersect M] if and only if [exists q in I+ and t0 in [0,T) with the tail gamma([t0,T)) subset J^-(q) intersect M]. Negating both sides: the whole-curve clause 'not exists q in I+ with gamma subset J^-(q) intersect M' in quantifiers.formal is logically equivalent to the tail clause 'for every q in I+ and every t0 in [0,T), the tail is not contained in J^-(q) intersect M' in visibility.negation_conclusion.
hypotheses: the causal relation used to define J^-(q) is the standard future-directed causal-precedence relation of the conformal completion (Mtilde, gtilde)
causal precedence is transitive (concatenation of future-directed causal curves is a future-directed causal curve)
gamma is future-directed causal, so for t < t0 the segment gamma|[t,t0] is a future-directed causal curve from gamma(t) to gamma(t0)
targets_under_test.proof: Fix t in [0,t0). By hypothesis gamma(t0) is in J^-(q), so gamma(t0) precedes q. The segment gamma|[t,t0] is a future-directed causal curve from gamma(t) to gamma(t0). By transitivity gamma(t) precedes q, hence gamma(t) is in J^-(q). Points with t >= t0 are in J^-(q) by hypothesis. Therefore gamma([0,T)) is a subset of J^-(q). The converse is immediate with t0 = 0.
targets_under_test.statement: Let q be a point of the conformal completion and let gamma: [0,T) -> M be a future-directed causal curve. If some tail gamma([t0,T)) is contained in J^-(q) intersect M for some t0 in [0,T), then the whole curve gamma([0,T)) is contained in J^-(q) intersect M.
